advisory.summary: server-side request forgery: a Spring @RestController reaches UrlServiceImpl.fetch through an @Autowired interface field; the sink issues an outbound request with no allowlist

acquisition.notes: Patched variant of the Spring Java SSRF repro: UrlServiceImpl.fetch enforces an allowlist (only 'public') via resolveTarget, rejecting 'internal' before any seed read or outbound request. The @RestController-to-interface-to-impl call graph is preserved; only the sink's runtime allowlist forecloses the exfiltration.

expected_verdict.label: reasoned_not_exploitable
expected_verdict.rationale: resolveTarget in UrlServiceImpl enforces an allowlist before the outbound request, so the CWE-918 SSRF sink is code-foreclosed for the exfiltrating target. The controller-to-service call path is preserved (static_taint_path_complete) but the guarded implementation is not exploitable; reasoned rather than proven because PoNE requires the two-trace. KnownGap: this row is surfaced in the corpus but not yet measured end-to-end -- until PLAN-020's per-language dispatch and this lane's populated symbol lists and ground truth land, the fixture Loads and Validates cleanly but the stub pipeline emits a uniform verdict, so direction/strength equality is not asserted (assertable_now=false), mirroring the symboltest harness's documented gap.
